metadata.note: Light rail in Minneapolis and St. Paul. The Hiawatha Line — now the METRO Blue Line — opened on 26 June 2004 between downtown Minneapolis and Fort Snelling, the first modern light rail in Minnesota, and the Central Corridor Green Line linked the two downtowns on 14 June 2014. Both are drawn in one Metro Transit colour under Rule 4, despite the agency's Blue and Green branding. Also here is the Como–Harriet Streetcar Line, a surviving fragment of the Twin City Rapid Transit system that the Minnesota Streetcar Museum has run as a heritage operation since 1971 — a genuine passenger service under Rule 1, tagged tourist_rail.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Como%E2%80%93Harriet_Streetcar_Line (museum operation on former Twin City Rapid Transit right of way)

metadata.not_yet_sourced: All headways and speeds are estimates; no timetable was consulted. The Como–Harriet relation traces only 0.64 mi against roughly a mile of surviving track, so the drawn line is short of the operating railway. The Northstar commuter line to Big Lake is NOT in this layer — no OSM route relation was found for it in the bbox searched, and its post-2020 service status was not established.
